notes: Raccoon fur. v2 moves it OFF the cardboard's hue: v1 measured a mean head hue of 22-30deg against the box front face at 23deg, so heads and vehicle were one material to the eye and the pair read as two teddy bears in a brown box. A raccoon is a grizzled grey-brown, so the shadow and base stops are now cool — violet-grey, sat ~0.15-0.19, well clear of the box's 0.6 at 36deg — while the LIT and TOP stops stay warm, which is the ART_BIBLE rule ('light warms hue ~50deg toward yellow and raises value') rather than a compromise. rimStrength came down from 0.9 because a 0.9 sky rim on a 0.29 m sphere floods the whole head and washes out the brush; detailStrength is up so the stroke relief survives on a curved surface the way it does on the flat box face.
